slides.title: 3.1 Understanding Contiguous Memory Layout
keyPoints: Contiguous storage places elements next to one another in the array’s element order.
An index maps to an element offset, supporting constant-time random access under the ordinary address-arithmetic.
The layout is valuable not only for indexing but also for traversing data with predictable nearby accesses.

slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 3, treat 3.1.1 Mapping Indices to Addresses as an algorithmic claim. For an array base and valid index i, the conceptual address offset is i * sizeof(T) bytes within the appropriate object representation. C++ pointer arithmetic performs element stepping directly, so code uses data[i] or data + i rather than manually inventing byte offsets for typed access. A dynamic owner must preserve the invariant size <= capacity and ensure the active sequence’s indices are below size. Capacity describes available storage, while size describes the logical sequence. In this integer-only teaching implementation, the allocated array actually constructs all capacity integers; that differs from a fully generic vector managing raw capacity without live elements in every slot. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. slides.title: Failure clinic — A count survived after its storage moved
keyPoints: A moved-from object reports size one thousand but has a null owning pointer.
The likely defect is a defaulted memberwise move that transferred the smart pointer but copied scalar metadata.
The smart pointer did its own job correctly; the class failed to preserve its combined invariant.
Repair the move operation or redesign the representation so the invariant follows automatically.
slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 3, treat Failure clinic — A count survived after its storage moved as an algorithmic claim. A moved-from object reports size one thousand but has a null owning pointer. The likely defect is a defaulted memberwise move that transferred the smart pointer but copied scalar metadata. The smart pointer did its own job correctly; the class failed to preserve its combined invariant. Repair the move operation or redesign the representation so the invariant follows automatically. A second failure appears only when appending an existing element at a capacity boundary. Examine whether an input reference points into the old buffer and whether it is read after reallocation. Testing push_back(42) repeatedly will not expose that alias. The supplied scalar-by-value interface intentionally avoids it. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran.
